newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. honours Frenchman for D-Day anniversary role.
newsitem.headline: U.S. honours Frenchman for D-Day anniversary role.

text.p: The U.S. Army is honouring Frenchman Henri-Jean Renaud for his help in welcoming thousands of Allied soldiers who returned to Normandy for the 50th anniversary of D-Day, a U.S. veterans group said on Tuesday.
The 82nd Airborne C-47 Historical Committee said Renaud would be awarded the U.S. medal for Distinguished Civilian Service at a ceremony on Wednesday at the U.S. embassy in Paris.
It said Renaud had performed outstanding work on behalf of veterans returning to his Normandy town of Sainte Mere-Eglise for the June 6, 1994, ceremonies marking the D-Day anniversary.

"I am extremely flattered because I am being thanked for what I have done for the past several years in welcoming returning allied soldiers," Renaud, the son of a former mayor of the town, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"It was important to show that we would not forget," he said.

Sainte Mere-Eglise was the first French village to be liberated from Nazi occupiers when some 15,000 paratroopers and glider-borne soldiers from the U.S. 82nd and 101st airborne divisions landed in the area during the night of June 5-6, 1944.
